title: The tenth of Muharram
hook: Husayn and his companions and family are killed on the day of Ashura

segments.voice: Yesterday, the river cut off: a camp at Karbala within sight of the Euphrates, and soldiers between them and the water. Your line was: they were thirsty. Did you pause before you drank? Day eight hundred ninety-one.

Before Karbala, the tenth day of Muharram already had a name: Ashura. Bukhari records that when the Prophet, peace be upon him, came to Medina, he found the Jews of the city fasting on that day, remembering how God had saved Moses and his people. The Prophet fasted it too, and asked his followers to fast. So it was a day of rescue, kept with a fast. Then came a morning on a plain beside the Euphrates, and the same day gained a second memory, this one of grief. Today: the tenth of Muharram.
screen: `ASHURA ALREADY HAD A NAME.` → `A DAY OF RESCUE.` → `THEN A SECOND MEMORY.`

segments.voice: The histories tell the morning slowly, and it's right to tell it plainly. Husayn's small band faces the army. One man rides out from the army's ranks and crosses over. It is al-Hurr, the commander who first blocked Husayn's road, and whose horses Husayn had watered. He asks if there is any repentance for him, and fights at Husayn's side. Then, through the day, the companions fall one by one. Then the young men of the family: sons, nephews, brothers. Tradition counts seventy-two in all who died with him. And at the last, Husayn himself, thirsty, is killed. The women and children are taken captive, among them his sister Zaynab, and his son Ali, who was too sick to fight. Sunni and Shia Muslims both honor Husayn. Sunni Muslims honor him as the Prophet's grandson, and Sunni practice keeps the Ashura fast from the Prophet's own example. For Shia Muslims, Husayn is the third Imam, and the tenth is the center of the year's mourning: gatherings, elegies, tears, the story told again so that it is never told for the last time. The Qur'an speaks to those who fall in God's way. In Pickthall's translation: "And call not those who are slain in the way of Allah 'dead.' Nay, they are living, only ye perceive not." Shia tradition reads Karbala in the light of that verse. And so one date carries two memories, a people rescued and a family falling, and both are kept. The tenth day.
screen: `AL-HURR CROSSES OVER.` · `ONE BY ONE, THEN HUSAYN.` · `SUNNI AND SHIA BOTH HONOR HIM.` · `NAY, THEY ARE LIVING.` · then, large: `THE TENTH DAY.`

segments.voice: The practice: sit in silence for them. There's nothing to do in this one, and nothing to fix. Settle, and breathe. Let the names you heard today come and go: al-Hurr, al-Abbas, Zaynab, Husayn. You don't need to feel anything in particular. Just keep them company for a little while, the way people sit with a family after a death. If you pray, you can say, as the Qur'an teaches, we are Allah's and unto Him we are returning. If you don't, just keep the quiet. The bell holds the time.
The tenth of Muharram. Ashura: the day the Prophet fasted for Moses' rescue, and the day Husayn and his companions were killed at Karbala. Today's word.

Your line: the tenth day. Today, keep one quiet minute somewhere ordinary, a car, a queue, a sink, and spend it remembering someone who died for what they would not give up. Day eight hundred ninety-one.

howItsDone: On the tenth of Muharram, Shia Muslims gather to mourn Husayn with elegies and recitations of Karbala; Sunni Muslims honor him too, and Sunni communities keep the Ashura fast that the Prophet kept.

Index hook gives 'seventy-two companions and family' and 'in 680'; the year is cut under the claims rule and the number is framed as 'tradition counts seventy-two'. Confirm a Keeper is comfortable with that framing.
Practice paraphrases Qur'an 2:156 without quotation marks; it is a Qur'anic phrase, not a new prayer.
'Many keep the Ashura fast' (Sunni practice) is a broad claim; confirm or soften.
'Shia Muslims read Karbala in the light of that verse': broad; confirm or cut 'and many others'.
Ali (Zayn al-Abidin) being too sick to fight is the standard account; confirm.
Audit: the hook's circular line 'a second memory, one that would be grieved for as long as it is remembered' became 'a second memory, this one of grief'.

Editor: 'a sea opening' is not in Bukhari 2004 (which says only that God saved Moses and his people), so it became 'a day of rescue, kept with a fast' and 'a people rescued'; 'Sunni and Shia Muslims both grieve this day' (a sweeping claim) became 'both honor Husayn', with the screen head to match; 'Shia Muslims read Karbala' became 'Shia tradition reads'.
